# --description--

Since `contains`, `hasPrefix` and `hasSuffix` return booleans, they combine naturally with `||` and `&&` to build more complex checks.

# --instructions--

Write a function `isImage` that takes a file name as a `String` (omit the argument label) and returns `true` when the name ends with `.png` or `.jpg`

# --before-seed--

```swift
// DO NOT EDIT FROM HERE
import Foundation

var _testCount = 0
var _testFailedCount = 0
func tryCatch(_ assertion: Bool) {
    _testCount += 1
    if !assertion {
        _testFailedCount += 1
        print("Test Case '--err-t\(_testCount)--' failed")
    }
}
// DO NOT EDIT UNTIL HERE
```

# --asserts--

`isImage("photo.png")` must return `true`

```swift
tryCatch(isImage("photo.png") == true)
```

`isImage("scan.jpg")` must return `true`

```swift
tryCatch(isImage("scan.jpg") == true)
```

`isImage("notes.txt")` must return `false`

```swift
tryCatch(isImage("notes.txt") == false)
```

`isImage("png")` must return `false`

```swift
tryCatch(isImage("png") == false)
```

`isImage("photo.png.bak")` must return `false`

```swift
tryCatch(isImage("photo.png.bak") == false)
```

# --after-asserts--

```swift
print("Executed \(_testCount) tests, with \(_testFailedCount) failures")
```

# --solutions--

```swift
func isImage(_ fileName: String) -> Bool {
    return fileName.hasSuffix(".png") || fileName.hasSuffix(".jpg")
}
```
